baseline.description: A perturbation changes expression by the sum of its genes' single-gene changes in training (additive model).

lineage.hypothesis: RIDGE on the baseline features plus the built-in sum of each target gene's single-gene training change.
Adding a feature that captures the co-expression similarity between the perturbation target gene(s) and the predicted gene g improves prediction of delta.
Drop mean_response from the best model (EXP_0014) to test whether it still earns its place.
Drop control_mean from the best model (EXP_0024) to test whether it still earns its place.
A feature that multiplies target coexpression by the target's replogle magnitude captures stronger downstream effects for strongly activated targets.
Drop target_coexpression_e14 from the best model (EXP_0058) to test whether it still earns its place.

Adding a feature that multiplies the sign-corrected replogle delta of the perturbation target(s) by the coexpression between gene g and the target(s) will improve predictions by capturing whether coexpressed genes are expected to be up- or down-regulated.
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=100 for the best model (EXP_0089).
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=300 for the best model (EXP_0101).
The product of additive_response and weighted_target_coexpression_e58 captures cases where coexpressed genes amplify the additive effect, improving prediction.
Drop weighted_target_coexpression_e58 from the best model (EXP_0121) to test whether it still earns its place.
The product of additive_response and the mean control expression of the target genes captures whether highly expressed targets produce larger changes.
The mean control expression level of the perturbation's target genes is predictive of delta[p,g].
Adding the square of additive_response to the current best feature set captures nonlinear scaling of perturbation effects.
Clipping additive_response to a reasonable range (e.g., [-0.5, 0.5]) reduces influence of outliers and improves generalization.
The sum of sign-corrected replogle deltas of PPI neighbors of gene g, weighted by inverse PPI distance or edge weight, is predictive of delta[p,g].
For pair perturbations, the product of coexpression between gene g and each target captures synergistic effects beyond additive response.
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=0.01 for the best model (EXP_0250).
Propagating additive_response over the PPI network (e.g., one-step weighted average) improves prediction over raw additive_response.
Interaction between additive_response and signed_replogle_coexpression improves prediction.
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=100 for the best model (EXP_0296).
Drop additive_times_coexpression_e121 from the best model (EXP_0311) to test whether it still earns its place.
A random Fourier feature projection of additive_response and signed_replogle_coexpression_e89 can capture nonlinear interactions that linear models miss.
For pair perturbations A+B, the product of sign-corrected replogle deltas of A and B for gene g captures multiplicative interaction and improves prediction.
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=100 for the best model (EXP_0361).
The number of gene sets containing both gene g and any target of p, normalized by total gene sets containing g, improves prediction.

Adding the product of additive_response and pair_replogle_delta_product_e361 improves prediction by capturing cases where the additive effect is modulated by the sign-corrected Replogle deltas of both targets.
For pair perturbations, the sum of sign-corrected Replogle deltas of the two targets provides additional predictive power beyond the product.
For each (p,g), additive_response multiplied by the inverse of the shortest path length from g to any target in PPI captures distance-dependent effects.
Removing pair_replogle_delta_product_e361 from the best model does not reduce performance, indicating redundancy.
Multiplying additive_response by pair_replogle_delta_product_e361 creates an interaction that may capture synergistic effects of target genes.
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=100 for the best model (EXP_0560).
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=300 for the best model (EXP_0593).
Drop additive_times_signed_replogle_coexpress_e296 from the best model (EXP_0606) to test whether it still earns its place.
Drop target_control_expression_mean_e167 from the best model (EXP_0643) to test whether it still earns its place.
For pair perturbations A+B, the product of PPI edge confidences along the shortest path between A and B (or 0 if disconnected) improves prediction.

most_useful_features.description: Product of sign-corrected Replogle deltas of the target genes for each gene g.
Elementwise product of additive_response and pair_replogle_delta_product_e361 for each (perturbation, gene).
Average over p's targets t of sign-corrected replogle delta of t times control Pearson correlation between gene g and t.
Average over p's targets of (control Pearson corr of g with target) times sign-corrected replogle delta of the target.
Elementwise product of additive_response and the mean control expression of p's target genes.
Elementwise product of additive_response and weighted_target_coexpression_e58.
Elementwise product of additive_response and signed_replogle_coexpression_e89.
Product of control-cell coexpression of gene g with each of p's targets (squared for singles).
For pair perturbations A+B, product of PPI edge confidences along the shortest path between A and B; 1 for singles, 0 if disconnected.
For pair perturbations, sum of sign-corrected Replogle deltas of the two target genes; for single-gene perturbations, equal to the target's delta.
